items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Glyn was a red head cat that sang a Frank Sinatra style, but I had never met him before.

ctx.x: Casablanca reminded me very much of Egypt as concerned the weather and the way the Moroccans dressed. In Egypt, the women wore black djellabas and covered their faces with black veils. Those in Morocco were djellabas of different colours and covered their faces with different coloured veils. You could only see their eyes. There were no difference in the way that the native men dressed in both countries. Some wore djellabas, some were dressed like the men in European countries. The women in Egypt and Morroco who…

The 23rd we did a concer in Rabat and then came back to Casablanca to play as an attraction in a place called "l'As des Clubs"(the ace of clubs). To say a few words about the musicians, I had known Blareau and Aubert in Paris and they were both fine young musicians who played good jazz. The pianist was good also and knew how to accompany a soloist. Glyn was a red head cat that sang a Frank Sinatra style, but I had never met him before.

At the Ace of Clubs, there was a giant size Arab who was the doorman and he spoke very good English. We became quite friendly that night. And as I liked a little taste of gage now and then, and was also aware that I was in a country where I could get some good stuff, I hit on this fellow and he was more than happy to get me a supply. The next night he had a nice package for me and some of the other musicians who also liked a taste now and then were my guests.
